ruling_summary: Established that law enforcement must inform suspects of their rights before interrogation
key_points: 1. Right to remain silent (Fifth Amendment). 2. Statements can be used against you. 3. Right to attorney. 4. If you cannot afford attorney, one will be provided.

ruling_summary: Right to counsel is fundamental and must be provided to poorest defendants
key_points: 1. Sixth Amendment guarantees right to counsel. 2. States must provide attorneys to indigent defendants. 3. Access to justice is fundamental right.

ruling_summary: Right to privacy includes a woman's decision to have an abortion (later overturned)
key_points: 1. Privacy rights under Due Process Clause. 2. Trimester framework established. 3. State can restrict abortion in later trimesters.

ruling_summary: School segregation based on race violates Equal Protection Clause
key_points: 1. Separate educational facilities are inherently unequal. 2. De jure segregation violates 14th Amendment. 3. Overruled Plessy v. Ferguson.

ruling_summary: Established judicial review; courts can strike down unconstitutional laws
key_points: 1. Judicial review is constitutional power of courts. 2. Constitution is supreme law. 3. Courts enforce constitutional limits on government power.

ruling_summary: Maximum work hour law unconstitutional (later overturned); liberty of contract
key_points: 1. Due Process includes economic liberty. 2. State cannot restrict working hours without rational basis. 3. Later rejected in West Coast Hotel v. Parrish.

ruling_summary: Separate but equal doctrine; racial segregation lawful if facilities equal (overturned)
key_points: 1. Separate accommodations don't violate 14th Amendment if equal. 2. State police power permits segregation. 3. Later overruled by Brown v. Board.

ruling_summary: Death penalty as then administered constitutes cruel and unusual punishment
key_points: 1. Arbitrary application of death penalty is unconstitutional. 2. Temporary halt to executions nationwide. 3. Led to reformed capital punishment statutes.

ruling_summary: Death penalty constitutional if procedurally sound; permits resumption of executions
key_points: 1. Death penalty is not per se unconstitutional. 2. Procedural safeguards must prevent arbitrary imposition. 3. Bifurcated trial structure constitutionally adequate.

ruling_summary: Unlawfully obtained evidence inadmissible in state criminal trials (exclusionary rule)
key_points: 1. Fourth Amendment applies to states via 14th Amendment. 2. Illegally obtained evidence excluded from trial. 3. Remedies unconstitutional search practices.

case_name: State of Kerala v. N.M. Thomas
ruling_summary: Backward class classifications must be reasonable and based on relevant criteria
key_points: 1. Equal protection under Article 14. 2. Backward class reservations valid. 3. Unreasonable classifications invalid.

case_name: Kesavananda Bharti v. State of Kerala
ruling_summary: Basic structure doctrine; Constitution has unamendable basic features
key_points: 1. Parliament cannot amend basic structure. 2. Separation of powers is basic feature. 3. Fundamental rights are core to Constitution.

ruling_summary: Article 14 and 16 protections in employment and equality before law
key_points: 1. Equal protection in public employment. 2. Age qualifications must be reasonable. 3. Discrimination prohibited.

case_name: Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India
ruling_summary: Procedure established by law under Article 21 must be reasonable and just
key_points: 1. Expanded Article 21 right to life. 2. Fair procedure essential. 3. Right encompasses dignity and human rights.

ruling_summary: Government companies are state under Article 12 for constitutional purposes
key_points: 1. Public sector enterprises subject to Article 12. 2. Fundamental rights apply to government companies. 3. Extends constitutional protections.

case_name: S. R. Bommai v. Union of India
ruling_summary: President's power to dismiss state government under Article 356 is justiciable
key_points: 1. Judicial review of President's Article 356 power. 2. Safeguards against abuse of emergency powers. 3. Grounds for dismissal reviewable.

case_name: Indira Sawhney v. Union of India (Mandal case)
ruling_summary: Other Backward Classes reservations valid; creamy layer concept introduced
key_points: 1. Article 16(4) allows OBC reservations. 2. Creamy layer exclusion required. 3. 50% ceiling on total reservations.

ruling_summary: Parliament cannot amend fundamental rights by constitutional amendment
key_points: 1. Fundamental rights are immutable. 2. Later overruled by 24th Amendment. 3. Shift in constitutional jurisprudence.

ruling_summary: During emergency, court cannot issue habeas corpus; President powers supreme
key_points: 1. Emergency powers can override fundamental rights. 2. Limited during national emergency. 3. Controversial; eroded civil liberties.

case_name: Waman Rao v. Union of India
ruling_summary: Basic structure doctrine; certain constitutional amendments are unamendable
key_points: 1. Constitutional Amendments subject to basic structure test. 2. Sovereignty and federalism are basic features. 3. Checks on amendment power.

case_name: Olga Tellis v. Bombay Municipal Corporation
ruling_summary: Right to life includes right to livelihood and shelter
key_points: 1. Article 21 includes right to work. 2. Eviction requires due process. 3. Expands social and economic rights.

case_name: Peoples Union for Civil Liberties v. Union of India
ruling_summary: Public Interest Litigation expanded; environmental protection is fundamental duty
key_points: 1. Right to environment implicit in Article 21. 2. PIL mechanism for public grievances. 3. Precautionary principle applied.

ruling_summary: Sexual harassment at workplace; constitutional duty to prevent and remedy
key_points: 1. Sexual harassment violates rights. 2. Workplace safety guarantees. 3. Guidelines for employer responsibility.

case_name: MC Mehta v. Union of India
ruling_summary: Doctrine of absolute liability for hazardous substance operations
key_points: 1. Strict liability for toxic releases. 2. Enterprise must compensate victims. 3. Environmental protection paramount.

case_name: Bachan Singh v. State of Punjab
ruling_summary: Death penalty constitutional with restrictions on capital offenses and procedures
key_points: 1. Rarest of rare cases doctrine. 2. Mitigating circumstances considered. 3. Guided discretion required.

ruling_summary: Criminal intimidation and defamation; balance between free speech and protections
key_points: 1. Free speech not absolute. 2. Defamation and intimidation actionable. 3. Public persona reduced protection.

case_name: Shreya Singhal v. Union of India
ruling_summary: Section 66A IT Act (sedition clause) unconstitutional; protects free speech online
key_points: 1. Sedition clause too vague. 2. Free speech protected online. 3. Chilling effect on legitimate expression.

ruling_summary: Privacy rights under Constitution; personal autonomy protected
key_points: 1. Right to privacy implicit in Constitution. 2. Inviolable personal spaces. 3. Foundation for later privacy jurisprudence.

case_name: State of U.P. v. Rajendra Singh
ruling_summary: Circumstantial evidence standards; reasonable doubt and chain of circumstances
key_points: 1. Reasonable doubt standard applies. 2. Circumstantial evidence must form complete chain. 3. Burden on prosecution.

ruling_summary: Prison conditions and constitutional rights of inmates during detention
key_points: 1. Fundamental rights persist in prison. 2. Torture prohibited. 3. Dignity maintained in custody.
